correctness.rationale: The weak-test objective is exactly the quadratic form induced by the test-frame operator. In the explicit fixed-span two-test family, both tests have unit energy norm, ordinary Euclidean Gauss-Newton gives xi=1/epsilon exactly, and the true energy-error amplification is sqrt(1+epsilon^{-2}). The Gram spectrum gives the stated exact condition-number law, and the standalone artifact reproduces the formulas numerically.

originality.rationale: General basis dependence of variational residual losses, inverse-Gram discrete dual norms, minimum-residual methods, and tight-frame identities are prior knowledge and excluded from the novelty claim. The accepted contribution is narrowly source-specific: individual energy normalization in the 2026 weak Gauss-Newton construction still permits a fixed test span to produce an unboundedly harmful one-step correction, with an exact frame-conditioning amplification law. No equivalent public correction or overlapping SCOPE record was located.

value.rationale: The counterexample isolates test-frame conditioning, rather than individual test norms, as the quantity governing the geometry of ordinary Euclidean weak-residual Gauss-Newton. It supplies a concrete failure certificate for a very recent formulation and clarifies why unit normalization alone cannot provide basis robustness.
